We are given d(m) = 21. The divisors of 21 are (21, 1) and (7, 3). Thus, m must be of the form p^20 or p^6 * q^2 for distinct primes p and q. Since n < 10,000, m < 12,005. Also n > 0, so m > 2005. For m = p^20, 2^20 = 1,048,576 > 12,005, so no solutions exist. For m = p^6 * q^2: (1) If p=2, m = 64 * q^2. 2005 < 64q^2 < 12005 implies 31.3 < q^2 < 187.6. Possible primes q: {7, 11, 13}. Values of m: 64*49=3136, 64*121=7744, 64*169=10816. (2) If p=3, m = 729 * q^2. 2005 < 729q^2 < 12005 implies 2.75 < q^2 < 16.4. Possible primes q: {2}. Value of m: 729*4=2916. (3) If p=5, m = 15625 * q^2 > 12005. The possible values of m are {2916, 3136, 7744, 10816}. The values of n = m - 2005 are {911, 1131, 5739, 8811}. Sum = 911 + 1131 + 5739 + 8811 = 16592.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
